name: Islamic Republic of Iran

areaKm2.note: world_1960 Iran polygon = ~1,615,000 km2 computed on the sphere (low). Official area 1,648,195 km2 (mid/high). Iraqi-occupied strip of Khuzestan (from Sep 1980) not removed.

population.note: OWID (UN WPP) Iran 1980 = 39.84M; COW NMC v7 tpop 1980 = 39,291k; MB 1981-82 = 39,665,000; MB 1980-81 = 38,250,000 (low, older estimate).

urbanization.note: OWID urban share Iran 1980 = 50.7%. COW upop/tpop 1980 = 13,588/39,291 = 0.35 (cities over 100,000 only), not used for mid.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): total 195,000 (army 150,000 incl. 100,000 conscripts, navy 10,000, air force 35,000) + Revolutionary Guards (Pasdaran) ~30,000 in Sep 1980 (40,000 by mid-1981, MB 1981-82 para-military) = ~225,000. IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): 240,000 pre-1979. Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 110,000-215,000 soldiers. COW NMC v7 milper 1980 = 305,000 (high). Pasdaran counted inside active because it fought as a combat force from the first week; gendarmerie excluded.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): RESERVES 400,000 (former conscripts, high). Mid discounts for post-revolution disorganisation; Basij volunteers (formed Nov 1979) were untrained in Sep 1980 and are not counted.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the P roles: navy 10,000-20,000 and air force 35,000-70,000 (MB 1981-82 vs 1980-81) + army armour, artillery, aviation (~700 helicopters), HAWK battalions and logistics, ~60,000-70,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 600,000-850,000 soldiers in 1988 out of ~52M, plus Basij rotating through the front, so several million served over the war. Ratio of a total-war call-up 4-10% of population; Iran never mobilised to the levels of Iraq (COW milper peak).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): 4 armoured and 4 infantry 'divisions' (at least 2 of each only brigade strength). ~3 infantry divisions and the mech infantry of the armoured divisions at 50-60% strength after desertions = ~60,000 infantry. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: G3 rifles, TOW and Dragon ATGW (MB 1980-81) were modern 1970s Western kit.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 100,000 of 150,000 army personnel were conscripts (MB 1981-82); training collapsed in 1979-80 and 12,000 officers were purged (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): Pasdaran 40,000 by mid-1981 (~30,000 in Sep 1980) + the airborne / special forces brigade (~5,000). Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Pasdaran had small arms and RPGs only, no heavy weapons in 1980.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25 (militia). Evidence: Pasdaran were revolutionary militia; the airborne brigade (high) was professional.

count.note: Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 300-1,100 artillery pieces (low = operable). IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): 1,000+ guns/how incl. 330 M-101, 112 M-114, 440 M-109, 38 M-107, 14 M-110, 72 BM-21 MRL.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: M-109 and M-107/110 SP artillery modern for 1980.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 minus purge. Evidence: artillery branch less purged than armour; fire control weak.

count.note: Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 1,700-2,100 tanks, 500-1,150 operable. IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less) (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1980.shtml): 875 Chieftain, 400 M-47/-48, 460 M-60A1, 250 Scorpion = 1,985 (high). MB 1981-82: 620 Chieftain, 390 M-47/48, 400 M-60A1, 220 Scorpion after a year of losses. Mid = the operable fleet.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Chieftain Mk 3/5 and M-60A1 were front-line Western tanks of the late 1970s, degraded by missing spare parts and the US embargo.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Khuzestan had only a handful of operational company-size tank units (Iran-Iraq War article); crews and maintainers lost in the purge.

count.note: Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 1,000-1,900 armoured vehicles. IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): BMP MICV, about 325 M-113, 500 BTR-40/-50/-60/-152 APC.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mix of M-113 and old Soviet BTRs, a few BMP-1.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: see infantry.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): 4 sqn with 77 F-14A + 8 sqn with 166 F-5E/F = 243 (high). IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): F-14A perhaps 9 serviceable by mid-1981. Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 421-485 fighter-bombers, 200-205 fully operational in Sep 1980. Mid ~ half the inventory.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (F-14A with AWG-9 and Phoenix the best interceptor in the region) minus serviceability. Evidence: MB 1980-81 lists Phoenix, Sidewinder, Sparrow AAM.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: US-trained pilots, some purged and jailed, released to fly after the invasion; air force showed its power in 1980 strikes (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): 10 FGA sqn with 188 F-4D/E (high); 14 RF-4E excluded. IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): 90 F-4D/E, perhaps 50 serviceable, by mid-1981. Mid ~60% serviceable in Sep 1980: the day after the invasion Iran struck air bases, refineries and Baghdad in the large-scale Operation Kaman 99 (Iran-Iraq War article).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: F-4E with Maverick and laser-guided bombs; 707/747 tankers gave reach.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: as fighters.

count.note: Iran-Iraq War infobox, start of war (Pollack p. 186-187; Razoux 2015; Farrokh 2011 p. 304-305): 750-835 helicopters, 240 fully operational. IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): army 205 AH-1J, 295 Bell 214A, 50 AB-205A, 20 AB-206, 90 CH-47C; plus air force and naval helicopters.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: AH-1J with TOW and CH-47C among the era's best, if serviceable.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: Army Aviation Command remained effective in close support (Iran-Iraq War article).

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): 3 destroyers (1 ex-British Battle, 2 ex-US Sumner) with Standard SSM, 4 Saam (Vosper Mk 5) frigates with Seakiller SSM and Seacat SAM = 7; same in MB 1981-82.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Saam frigates modern; destroyers WWII hulls with missile refits.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: navy halved (20,000 to 10,000) after the revolution.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 1980-1981, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription; the edition flags that pre-1979 manpower and holdings are shown and present totals are considerably less): 4 ex-US PF-103 corvettes, 9 Kaman (La Combattante II) FAC(M) with Harpoon, 7 large patrol craft, 5 minesweepers = 25; high adds 14 hovercraft. MB 1981-82: 7 Kaman.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Harpoon-armed Kaman FAC led Operation Morvarid (Nov 1980), which destroyed 80% of the Iraqi navy (Iran-Iraq War article).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: as major ships.

count.note: Batteries. IISS Military Balance 1981-1982, Iran entry (samlib.ru transcription, post-losses estimates): 4 army SAM battalions with HAWK/Improved HAWK (~12-16 batteries); air force 5 SAM sqn with Rapier and 25 Tigercat (~10-15 fire-unit batteries); 1,800 towed AA guns (ZU-23, 35 mm, 40 mm, 57 mm, 85 mm) + 100 ZSU-23-4/ZSU-57-2 at 6-8 guns per battery = ~240-300 batteries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Improved HAWK and Rapier were modern Western SAMs; much AAA older.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 minus purge. Evidence: HAWK crews US-trained; spare parts lacking.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25 (ad hoc, poor coordination). Evidence: 85 senior generals executed Feb-Sep 1979 and ~12,000 officers purged by Sep 1980 (Iran-Iraq War article); rival chains of command between the army and the Pasdaran under President Banisadr.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: army units at half strength after desertions, distrusted by the clergy; Pasdaran cohesive but improvised.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (motivated) toward 1.0 (fanatical or existential defence). Evidence: revolutionary fervour and defence of the homeland against invasion; volunteers flooded in, Khorramshahr held for over a month.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: TOW, Dragon, Phoenix, Harpoon, Maverick, Improved HAWK (MB 1980-81): late-1970s Western guided weapons.

armor.note: Anchor: below 9 (composite armour). Evidence: Chieftain Mk 5 and M-60A1 with steel armour; the Shir Iran (Challenger precursor) order was cancelled in 1979.

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: Saam frigates and Harpoon-armed FAC; no submarines (Tang order cancelled).

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 = concrete lines. Evidence: some hardened aircraft shelters at main bases; no prepared border defences in Khuzestan.

logistics.note: Anchor: between 8 (motor transport) and 9 (airlift). Evidence: 54 C-130, 12 Boeing 707 and 8 Boeing 747 tanker/transports, 80-90 CH-47C (MB 1981-82); spare-parts collapse under embargo.

communications.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: US-built microwave and tropo-scatter military network; no satellite communications.

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar, 9 = satellites. Evidence: F-14 AWG-9 used as mini-AWACS, P-3F maritime patrol, RF-4E; no satellites.

air.note: Anchor: air 9 = 1985. Evidence: F-14A Tomcat (fourth generation), F-4E, inflight refuelling.

cyber.note: No military computer networks with attack capability before ~1985; anchor cyber 9 = 1990 networks.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison 2023 (OWID CSV) Iran 1980 = 6,334 (2011 int$); 1979 = 7,678 (high), 1981 = 5,887 (low); 1977 = 10,205 before the revolutionary collapse.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via OWID: Iran 1980 = 5.34% (low, mostly peacetime months), 1981 = 8.19% (high, first full war year); 1978 = 11.1% under the Shah. Mid for the wartime run rate in late 1980.

industrialShare.note: World Bank NV.IND.TOTL.ZS (industry incl. oil, % GDP): 1980 = 35.2%, 1979 = 45.8%, 1981 = 34.7%.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Iran 1980 = 45.6%. CIA World Factbook 1990: 33% (1988). Share 45.6% (range 40.0-50.0%) -> 0.544 (0.5-0.6).

annualCohort.note: World Bank 1980 (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y, SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN): male pop 20,500,870 x 10.53% / 5 = ~431,700 males per year. CIA World Factbook 1990: 569,647 males reach military age (21) annually (a later, larger cohort). audit 2026-10-30: males only, the conscript-pool convention of all other snapshots (derived:cohort-from-agegroup applied to the male term only); was 832,000 for both sexes.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: CIA World Factbook 1990 (https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/14/pg14.txt) gives 42,566 km bituminous and 46,866 km gravel/crushed stone roads in 1990 (high = sum); the 1980 network was smaller.

railKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iran entry: railroads 4,601 km total in 1990 with 730 km (Bafq-Bandar Abbas) still under construction, so the 1980 network was ~4,500 km.

majorPorts.note: CIA World Factbook 1990 (Project Gutenberg #14), Iran entry lists Abadan, Bandar Beheshti (Chabahar), Bandar Abbas, Bushehr, Bandar Khomeyni, Bandar Shahid Rajai, Khorramshahr; Abadan and Khorramshahr were in the 1980 battle zone (low). Plus Kharg Island oil terminal.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: National Iranian Tanker Co. and IRISL fleets of ~1.5M GRT in 1980 x 1.5 dwt/grt. CIA World Factbook 1990 gives 8,662,454 DWT for 1990, after the wartime tanker build-up.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: Iranian logistics in 1980 could barely move divisions to Khuzestan; the 1981-82 counter-offensives reached ~100-150 km from railheads at Ahvaz and Dezful.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: donkeys (~1.8M), horses, mules and camels in a large rural economy; mules used by mountain units in Kurdistan.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS stockpile series (OWID) lists no Iranian warheads; the Shah's nuclear power programme was halted in 1979.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified cities (Khorramshahr, Abadan held), strong population support; high 1.3 for the Zagros barrier and strategic depth behind Khuzestan.

notes: Snapshot date 22 September 1980 (Iraqi invasion). The IISS Military Balance 1980-81 (data July 1980) reprinted pre-revolution holdings and said present totals were considerably less; the 1981-82 edition shows post-losses holdings. Equipment counts therefore span operable (low, Pollack and Razoux via the Iran-Iraq War infobox) to nominal inventory (high); mid is the operable-plus-repairable fleet. Personnel: active = regular army, navy, air force + Pasdaran (~30,000, fought as combat troops from the start); Basij and gendarmerie excluded; reservists (400,000 ex-conscripts per MB) in trainedReserves. Population and territory: Iran within its 1980 borders; Iraqi-occupied parts of Khuzestan not removed. Logistics bounds come from the 1990 CIA World Factbook and are shifted down for 1980 by judgement (grade D where stated). No domestic production of major platforms in 1980 (production {}).
